machine: 12th Gen Intel Core i9-12900HK, Linux 7.0.11 x86_64, NVMe
notes: hive_ce_web rows: Hive CE chromium 151.0.7922.108 (/usr/bin/google-chrome), IndexedDB, 20 iterations, median/p99.

crossbank_indexeddb_web rows: tests/bench_web.rs in chrome, cargo profile --release, ONE un-warmed shot (Criterion does not run in wasm), so p99 is null and these are noisier than the Hive rows. It times with Date.now() (1 ms resolution), so a sub-millisecond per-op loop reads as 0 / null ops_per_s.
Both lanes drove the SAME browser binary: /usr/bin/google-chrome 151.0.7922.108 (Playwright executablePath for the Hive lane, chromedriver for the wasm lane).

The *_web_small rows are the only apples-to-apples pair today: tests/bench_web.rs uses 50 settings keys / 200 bulk ops, so bench/hive_ce/web mirrors those shapes exactly. Unifying bench_web.rs onto the large shapes is the remaining Phase 5 item.

crossbank_indexeddb_web run-to-run spread over three runs: bulk_lazy_put_web_small 33-49 ms, bulk_lazy_get_web_small 16-27 ms. One un-warmed shot is noisy; treat these as an order of magnitude, not a point estimate.

Neither side is fsync-durable here. IndexedDB durability is browser-dependent (Chromium defaults its transactions to 'relaxed'), so a Hive put and a crossbank put on the web are on comparable footing - unlike the native table, where crossbank commits durably and Hive does not.
